question: A 72-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of severe, acute, right leg pain for 2 hours. The patient's symptoms started suddenly while he was doing household chores. He has no history of leg pain at rest or with exertion. Yesterday, he returned home after a 6-hour bus ride from his grandson's home. He has hypertension treated with ramipril. He appears uncomfortable. His temperature is 37.4°C (99.3°F), pulse is 105/min and irregular, and blood pressure is 146/92 mm Hg. The right lower extremity is cool and tender to touch. A photograph of the limb is shown. Femoral pulses are palpable bilaterally; popliteal and pedal pulses are decreased on the right side. Sensation to pinprick and light touch and muscle strength are decreased in the right lower extremity. Which of the following is most likely to confirm the underlying source of this patient's condition?

paths: (Blood Circulation)-PROCESS_OF->(Structure of cortex of kidney)-LOCATION_OF->(Doppler Ultrasound)
(Blood Circulation)-PROCESS_OF->(Structure of cortex of kidney)-LOCATION_OF->(Doppler Ultrasound)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "72-year-old man with acute right leg pain" -> "sudden onset of symptoms after prolonged immobility" -> "possible deep vein thrombosis or embolism" -> "cool and tender right lower extremity" -> "decreased pulses in the right leg" -> "indicates compromised blood flow" -> "Doppler ultrasonography can assess blood flow" -> "most likely to confirm the underlying source" -> 85%

CHAIN: "72-year-old man with acute right leg pain" -> "history of prolonged bus ride" -> "risk factor for venous thromboembolism" -> "cool and tender right lower extremity" -> "decreased sensation and muscle strength" -> "suggests acute limb ischemia" -> "Doppler ultrasonography can evaluate for occlusion" -> "most likely to confirm the underlying source" -> 90%

enhanced_information: The 72-year-old man presents with acute right leg pain, coolness, tenderness, and decreased pulses, suggesting acute limb ischemia likely due to embolism, especially after prolonged immobility. Doppler ultrasonography is the preferred non-invasive method to assess blood flow and identify occlusion in the leg, making it the most likely option to confirm the underlying source of his condition. Echocardiography, while useful for identifying cardiac sources of embolism, is less direct for limb assessment. Digital subtraction angiography, although it visualizes blood vessels, is invasive and not first-line for acute assessment. Therefore, Doppler ultrasonography is the most appropriate choice.
analysis: The patient presents with acute limb ischemia characterized by sudden onset of severe leg pain, coolness, tenderness, and diminished pulses in the right lower extremity. Given the context of recent prolonged immobility (6-hour bus ride), the most likely underlying cause is an embolism, possibly from a cardiac source. Doppler ultrasonography is the preferred non-invasive method to assess blood flow in the legs and can confirm the presence of occlusion or reduced blood flow. While echocardiography can identify potential sources of embolism, it does not directly assess the limb's vascular status. Digital subtraction angiography, although it provides detailed vascular imaging, is invasive and not the first-line investigation in acute settings. Therefore, Doppler ultrasonography is the most appropriate choice to confirm the underlying source of the patient's condition.
